$comment: Low Talk patch schema: the single source of truth for every synth parameter. Shared by the engine, language layer and UI. curve: linear | log (min > 0) | pow (value = min + (max-min)*t^exponent).

params.label: Polyphony
params.describes: 1 = monophonic (legato and glide work, the bass default). 2-8 = that many notes at once, for pads, keys and chords; the oldest note is taken over when more are played.

params.label: Legato
params.describes: On: overlapping notes slide without retriggering the envelopes (303-style). Off: every note retriggers.

params.label: Glide time
params.describes: Time to slide between notes. 0 is instant; 30-120 ms is a quick slide; above 300 ms is a slow swoop.

params.label: Octave
params.describes: Shifts the whole patch (oscillators and sub) by octaves.

params.label: Velocity sensitivity
params.describes: How much playing harder makes the sound louder. 0 ignores velocity.

params.label: Analog drift
params.describes: Analog character: each unison voice drifts slightly in pitch, unison phases start free, and the filter varies a touch per note. 0 is perfectly digital and static; 0.2-0.4 is a warm vintage synth; higher is loose and wobbly.

params.label: Mod wheel move
params.describes: What the mod wheel does, each move turning several connected things together. Pressure: like playing harder (louder, brighter, grittier, a little breath). Snarl: aggression (distortion, resonance and bite). Open: light comes in (filter and top open). Choke: darker, tighter, drier, narrower. Vibrato: a human vibrato. Unstable: a dying machine (wobble, detune, sag). Decay: the sound falls apart (wear, crush, grain). Bloom: it drifts away (reverb, delay, width, chorus).

params.label: Preset's own move
params.describes: The move this preset was designed with; used when the mod wheel move is set to preset default.

params.label: Osc 1 wave
params.describes: Sine is pure and round; triangle is soft with a little edge; saw is bright and buzzy; pulse is hollow and reedy; wavetable morphs with the position control; pwm_saw is the rave "hoover" saw-plus-pulse (move pulse width for the swirl); string is a plucked physical-model string (see String).

params.label: Osc 1 semitones
params.describes: Pitch offset in semitones. +12/-12 adds an octave layer; +7 adds a fifth for a harder, organ-like tone.

params.label: Osc 1 fine tune
params.describes: Fine detune in cents. Small offsets between the two oscillators cause slow beating (Reese movement).

params.label: Osc 1 pulse width
params.describes: Only for the pulse wave. 0.5 is a hollow square; values near the ends are thin and nasal.

params.label: Osc 1 wavetable position
params.describes: Only for the wavetable wave. Sweeps sine (0) → triangle → saw → square → vocal/formant (1). Higher is brighter and more complex.

params.label: Osc 1 unison voices
params.describes: Number of stacked, detuned copies. 1 is tight and focused; 3-7 is wide, thick and buzzy.

params.label: Osc 1 unison detune
params.describes: Spread of the unison copies in cents. Low is subtle thickening; high is a dissonant, washy smear.

params.label: Osc 1 stereo spread
params.describes: How far the unison copies are panned..

params.label: Osc 1 level
params.describes: Oscillator volume into the filter.

params.label: Osc 1 filter cutoff
params.describes: Cutoff of oscillator 1's own filter (its type is set next to it). As a high-pass (the default) it cuts the low end before the drive so the harmonics distort without muddying the sub's space; 20 Hz = off. As a low-pass, 20 kHz = open.

params.label: Osc 1 filter type
params.describes: Oscillator 1's own filter before the main filter: high-pass (24 or 12 dB) thins the low end, low-pass (24 or 12 dB) darkens just this layer, band keeps a band around the cutoff.

params.label: Osc 1 filter keytrack
params.describes: On: the cutoff follows the played note (set for C3), so the layer keeps the same tone across the keyboard. Off: a fixed frequency.

params.label: Osc 2 wave
params.describes: Sine is pure and round; triangle is soft with a little edge; saw is bright and buzzy; pulse is hollow and reedy; wavetable morphs with the position control; pwm_saw is the rave "hoover" saw-plus-pulse (move pulse width for the swirl); string is a plucked physical-model string (see String).

params.label: Osc 2 fine tune

params.label: Osc 2 pulse width

params.label: Osc 2 wavetable position

params.label: Osc 2 level

params.label: Osc 2 filter cutoff
params.describes: Cutoff of oscillator 2's own filter (its type is set next to it). As a high-pass (the default) it cuts the low end before the drive so the harmonics distort without muddying the sub's space; 20 Hz = off. As a low-pass, 20 kHz = open.

params.label: Osc 2 filter type
params.describes: Oscillator 2's own filter before the main filter: high-pass (24 or 12 dB) thins the low end, low-pass (24 or 12 dB) darkens just this layer, band keeps a band around the cutoff.

params.label: Osc 2 filter keytrack

params.label: Osc 2 hard sync
params.describes: Hard sync: oscillator 2 restarts its cycle every time oscillator 1 starts one. Tune or sweep oscillator 2's pitch above oscillator 1 for the classic tearing, vocal sync lead.

params.label: String tone
params.describes: For the string wave: how bright the pluck and the string are. Low is a dark, thumbed double bass; high is a bright, snappy pick.

params.label: String sustain
params.describes: For the string wave: how long the string rings, from a short muted thump to a long sustaining tone.

params.label: Sub wave
params.describes: Sine is pure weight; warm sine adds a touch of its octave, so it stays round but you hear it on small speakers (the modern 808 sub); triangle adds a little edge; square is hollow, buzzy weight; pulse (25%) is thinner and nasal (the Juno / SH-101 sub); saw is the richest, weight and edge under reeses and leads. All band-limited.

params.label: Sub octave
params.describes: The sub's octave against the played note, -4 to +4. -1 is the usual sub; -2 a very deep rumble; 0 and up turn it into a clean, mono sine (or triangle, square) layer at or above the note. Notes that would fall below 20 Hz fold up an octave.

params.label: Sub level
params.describes: Clean mono sub that bypasses filter and distortion. More is heavier low end you feel more than hear.

params.label: Sub clip
params.describes: Transparent soft clipper on the sub only: shaves its peaks (about 1.5 dB at 3, 2.5 dB at 6, 4 dB at 12) and adds density, while everything under the knee stays at the same level, so it sounds fuller, not louder. 0 = off.

params.label: Sub filter type
params.describes: The sub's own filter: low-pass takes the edge off a triangle or square sub, high-pass trims the deepest rumble. Off = untouched.

params.label: Sub filter cutoff
params.describes: Cutoff of the sub's own filter.

params.label: Sub filter keytrack
params.describes: On: the sub filter's cutoff follows the played note (set for C3).

params.label: Sub direct out
params.describes: On (the default): the sub skips dynamics, effects and EQ and only meets the output's safety stages. Off: it goes through the dynamics, effects and EQ with the rest.

params.label: Noise level
params.describes: White noise into the filter for grit, breath and attack texture. Keep low.

params.label: Texture type
params.describes: What the Noise strip plays. Grain: crackle (vinyl pops), dust (fine grit), static (grainy radio fizz). Noise: tape hiss, air (a broad breathy band), rumble (low and dark, kept above the sub). Grain and noise play under the whole note and linger for Tail. Hit: each of the six as one burst at each new note, fading over Tail, nothing between, harder notes bursting bigger; air hit is the breath (a puff on each note, for brass, flutes, bowed and blown sounds). No pitch and no rhythm in any of them. Every type plays at the same loudness. White noise is plain, straight-up white noise (Tone darkens it); white noise hit is one burst of it per note.

params.label: Texture level
params.describes: How loud the texture bed is. It swells in with each note and lingers for the tail; silent between notes.

params.label: Texture tone
params.describes: Darker (0) to brighter (1); for crackle also sparser to busier.

params.label: Texture density
params.describes: How much there is. On the grains how many: crackle a rare pop to a broken record, dust a few specks to grit, static a soft fizz to a crunchy one. On the noise how thick (how much of the range it fills): tape hiss thin to full, air a wisp to a wall, rumble a narrow growl to a heavy one. The hits do the same inside their burst. The middle is each type's classic sound.

params.label: Noise octave
params.describes: Plays the bed slower or faster, like tape (-6 to +2 octaves): down everything gets darker, slower and bigger (crackle becomes slow dark thumps, hiss sinks to rumble), up it gets smaller and quicker. With KEY on this is where middle C sits, and the notes move it from there.

params.label: Noise key
params.describes: Makes the noise playable: its speed follows the note like a sample played across the keyboard (middle C at the OCT setting, each octave up twice as fast, down half as fast), with glide and pitch bend sliding it (glide from a high note to a low one for a tape stop). The bed is shared, so with chords it follows the newest note.

params.label: Texture tail
params.describes: How long the texture lingers after a note ends; on the hit types, how long each burst lasts.

params.label: Texture pan
params.describes: Moves the texture bed left or right.

params.label: Texture direct out
params.describes: On: the bed skips dynamics, effects and EQ (dry, like a separate track). Off: it goes through them with the sound.

params.label: Texture filter type
params.describes: The bed's own filter: high-pass keeps it out of the low end, low-pass darkens it, band narrows it to a band.

params.label: Texture filter cutoff
params.describes: Cutoff of the bed's own filter.

params.label: Texture filter keytrack
params.describes: On: the bed's filter follows the newest note (set for C3).

params.label: Drive on
params.describes: Switches Drive on or off without losing its settings. Off also saves CPU.

params.label: Pre-filter drive
params.describes: Warm saturation before the filter. Adds harmonics and thickness; the filter then rounds them off.

params.label: Filter on
params.describes: Switches Filter on or off without losing its settings. Off also saves CPU.

params.label: Filter type
params.describes: Low-pass is the classic 4-pole bass filter; band-pass is nasal and thin; formant makes vowels; diode is the squelchy 18 dB 303 filter; notch carves a moving hole (grinding, phasey); comb rings at the cutoff pitch (metallic, robotic, growly); lpg is a West-Coast low-pass gate that closes with the note for woody, acoustic thumps; high-pass is a 4-pole high-pass that takes the bottom away (sweep it up to thin a sound out for a build or a radio-like break). sem is an Oberheim SEM-style 12 dB low-pass: softer and more open than the ladder, it keeps its bass when the resonance is up (pads, brass, keys).

params.label: Filter cutoff
params.describes: Lower is darker and rounder; below ~300 Hz becomes muffled. In formant mode it shifts the vowel up or down.

params.label: Filter resonance
params.describes: Emphasis at the cutoff. Higher is squelchy and vocal (acid); near the top it whistles.

params.label: Filter key tracking
params.describes: How much the cutoff follows the played note. 1 keeps the tone consistent across the keyboard; 0 makes high notes darker.

params.label: Filter envelope amount
params.describes: How far the mod envelope sweeps the cutoff, 6 octaves per unit, up to ±9.97 octaves: from fully left on the Cutoff dial (20 Hz) all the way to fully right (20 kHz). Positive gives a plucky "wow" at the start of each note.

params.label: Filter vowel
params.describes: Formant mode only: morphs through vowels A → E → I → O → U.

params.label: Accent
params.describes: 303-style accent: hard-played notes open the filter further, resonate more and hit louder.

params.label: Filter: osc 1 in
params.describes: Oscillator 1 goes through the drive and the main filter. Off: it skips them (the distortion, tape and the rest still apply).

params.label: Filter: osc 2 in
params.describes: Oscillator 2 goes through the drive and the main filter. Off: it skips them.

params.label: Filter: noise in
params.describes: The Noise strip goes through the main filter: a texture bed through a copy of it that follows the newest note, breath through the drive and the voice's own filter. Off: it skips them.

params.label: Filter: sub in
params.describes: The sub goes through the drive and the main filter, and from there through the rest of the voice and the effects. Off (the default): the sub stays on its own clean path.

params.label: Filter mix
params.describes: Blend of the unfiltered (driven) and the filtered sound. 1 = fully filtered.

params.label: Distortion on
params.describes: Switches Distortion on or off without losing its settings. Off also saves CPU.

params.label: Drive type
params.describes: The drive's character, as RUIN's: tape is soft and warm, its highs saturating first; tube thick with even harmonics; amp a driven amp through a 4x12 cab, a close mic and a small room; soft clip clean below its knee, rounding off the peaks. Then the hard ones: hard clip squares the peaks off flat; wavefold folds the wave back on itself, more folds the harder it is driven (metallic, glassy); rectify flips the bottom half up (the octave above, hollow and buzzy); downsample holds each sample longer as Drive goes up, down to 1/32 of the rate (gritty, aliased, digital); diode is lopsided, soft on top and clipping early below (snarling, uneven harmonics). Starved: a tube starved of current (the Culture Vulture trick): quiet parts sputter and gate, only the big swings get through, lopsided.

params.label: Drive
params.describes: How hard the distortion is pushed. More is dirtier, louder-feeling and more compressed.

params.label: Distortion mix
params.describes: Blend between clean and distorted signal.

params.label: Drive tone
params.describes: After the drive: low is dark and smooth, high keeps all the fizz (fully up = open).

params.label: Distortion clean below
params.describes: Everything below this frequency bypasses the distortion, so the low end stays clean and tight while the mids get dirty. 20 Hz distorts everything; 100-200 Hz is the classic modern "clean sub, dirty mids" bass.

params.label: Bitcrusher on
params.describes: Switches Bitcrusher on or off without losing its settings. Off also saves CPU.

params.label: Bitcrusher mix
params.describes: Blend of the bitcrushed / downsampled signal. Lo-fi, retro, digital grit. Use sparingly on general basses; great for synthwave, cyberpunk and lo-fi textures. Never touches the sub.

params.label: Bit depth
params.describes: Lower is harsher and noisier. 12-16 is subtle grit; 6-8 is crunchy; under 5 is broken and fizzy.

params.label: Downsample
params.describes: Sample-rate reduction factor. 1 is off; 2-4 adds a metallic, aliased edge; above 10 sounds like a broken toy.

params.label: Bitcrusher low cut
params.describes: The bitcrusher only works above this frequency; below it the sound passes clean. 20 Hz = the whole sound.

params.label: Tape on
params.describes: Switches Tape on or off without losing its settings. Off also saves CPU.

params.label: Tape wow & flutter
params.describes: Slow, wandering pitch wobble like an old tape machine. A little sounds vintage and alive; a lot sounds warped and seasick (cinematic, LORN-style).

params.label: Tape low cut
params.describes: The tape only works above this frequency; below it the sound passes clean. 20 Hz = the whole sound.

params.label: Mid clip
params.describes: Transparent soft clipper on oscillators 1 and 2 only (after the dirt chain and the amp, before the effects; the sub has its own): shaves spikes and adds density at the same level. 0 = off.

params.label: Clean lows after the dirt
params.describes: On: after the distortion, crush and tape, the oscillators get their low cut once more (at the lower of the two oscillators' low cuts), removing the rumble the dirt itself created. The sub is never touched.

params.label: Amp attack
params.describes: Fade-in time. Under 5 ms is punchy; longer is a swell.

params.label: Amp decay
params.describes: Time to fall to the sustain level. Short with low sustain makes a pluck.

params.label: Amp sustain
params.describes: Level while the key is held. 1 is a held organ-like bass; 0 is a pluck or 808 decay.

params.label: Amp release
params.describes: Fade-out after the key is released. Short is tight; long overlaps notes.

params.label: Amp attack curve
params.describes: How the attack bends (the small dot on the envelope's line). Up: fast first, then settling (analog). Middle: a straight line. Down: slow first, then rushing (a swell).

params.label: Amp decay curve
params.describes: How the decay bends (the small dot on the envelope's line). Up: fast first, then settling (analog). Middle: a straight line. Down: slow first, then rushing (a swell).

params.label: Amp release curve
params.describes: How the release bends (the small dot on the envelope's line). Up: fast first, then settling (analog). Middle: a straight line. Down: slow first, then rushing (a swell).

params.label: Filter envelope on
params.describes: Switches the filter envelope on or off without losing its settings. Off, it no longer sweeps the cutoff and its matrix rows do nothing.

params.label: Mod attack
params.describes: Rise time of the mod envelope.

params.label: Mod decay
params.describes: Time for the mod envelope to fall to sustain. Short is plucky; long is a slow sweep.

params.label: Mod sustain
params.describes: Mod envelope level while the key is held.

params.label: Mod release
params.describes: Mod envelope fall time after release.

params.label: Filter env attack curve
params.describes: How the attack bends (the small dot on the envelope's line). Up: fast first, then settling (analog). Middle: a straight line. Down: slow first, then rushing (a swell).

params.label: Filter env decay curve
params.describes: How the decay bends (the small dot on the envelope's line). Up: fast first, then settling (analog). Middle: a straight line. Down: slow first, then rushing (a swell).

params.label: Filter env release curve
params.describes: How the release bends (the small dot on the envelope's line). Up: fast first, then settling (analog). Middle: a straight line. Down: slow first, then rushing (a swell).

params.label: Vibrato on
params.describes: Switches Vibrato on or off without losing its settings. Off also saves CPU.

params.label: Vibrato depth
params.describes: Pitch wobble of a played note in cents, like a string player or singer. 10-25 is natural; more is wobbly.

params.label: Vibrato rate
params.describes: Vibrato speed; each note varies it slightly so a chord never wobbles in lockstep.

params.label: Vibrato delay
params.describes: Time after the note starts before the vibrato begins: notes start straight, then sing.

params.label: Vibrato fade-in
params.describes: How long the vibrato takes to reach full depth after its delay.

params.label: LFO 1 on
params.describes: Switches LFO 1 on or off without losing its settings. Off also saves CPU.

params.label: LFO 1 shape
params.describes: Sine and triangle are smooth wobbles; saws are rhythmic ramps; square jumps; sample & hold is random steps; wander is smooth random motion that never repeats. Bloom, drop and random run per note, each note on its own: bloom rises from 0 to full over one cycle and stays there (the slow bloom of a held note), drop falls from full to 0 over one cycle (808 drops, tape stops, plucks), random is a new random value at the start of every note, held for the note. Drift glides towards a new random point every 0.4-1.6 s at 1 Hz (the old Drift source); slow drift curves between random points every 2-6 s at 0.25 Hz (the old Slow drift); Rate scales both.

params.label: LFO 1 rate
params.describes: Speed when not tempo-synced. Under 1 Hz is slow drift; 2-8 Hz is wobble; above 10 Hz is buzz/growl. For bloom and drop: one cycle is the rise or fall time (0.25 Hz = 4 s).

params.label: LFO 1 tempo sync
params.describes: Locks the LFO to the tempo as a note length (1/8 is the classic dubstep wobble). "free" uses the rate in Hz.

params.label: LFO 1 retrigger
params.describes: On: the LFO restarts on every note, so each note moves the same way.

params.label: LFO 1 fade-in
params.describes: Time for the LFO to fade in after each note starts. Lets a note hit clean, then come alive.

params.label: Chorus mix
params.describes: Stereo chorus on everything above the low cut. Wider, lusher, more 80s.

params.label: Chorus depth
params.describes: How much the chorus wobbles. High is seasick; low is a subtle widening.

params.label: Chorus mode
params.describes: classic = a two-voice chorus (gentle, wobbly); ensemble = a three-voice string-machine ensemble (lush); hyper = six steadily detuned copies spread across the stereo field (Serum's Hyper: a supersaw thickness on the whole sound, the noise, FM and GRIND included). bbd = the Juno / Jupiter chorus: bucket-brigade delays swept in opposite directions, darker, slightly saturated and hissy. params.label: Phaser mix
params.describes: Sweeping notches for a swirling, jet-like movement.

params.label: Phaser rate
params.describes: Speed of the phaser sweep.

params.describes: Switches Flanger on or off without losing its settings. Off also saves CPU.

params.describes: Jet-like comb sweep on the upper range. Metallic movement and width.

params.label: Flanger rate
params.describes: Speed of the flanger sweep.

params.label: Flanger feedback
params.describes: Higher makes the flanger more resonant and metallic.

params.describes: Switches Delay on or off without losing its settings. Off also saves CPU.

params.label: Delay mix
params.describes: Tempo-synced ping-pong echoes on the upper range (the low end stays dry). Adds space, rhythm and width.

params.label: Delay time
params.describes: Echo spacing as a note length. 1/8D (dotted eighth) is the classic rhythmic delay.

params.label: Delay feedback
params.describes: How many repeats. Above 0.7 the echoes trail on for a long time.

params.label: Delay tone
params.describes: Brightness of the repeats. Low is dark, dubby and distant; high is bright and present.

params.label: Reverb on
params.describes: Switches Reverb on or off without losing its settings. Off also saves CPU.

params.label: Reverb mix
params.describes: Reverb on the upper range only (the sub stays dry). A touch adds space; a lot is cinematic and washed out.

params.label: Reverb type
params.describes: The space, in the dark, band-limited colour of the late-1970s digital reverbs. Room: small and quick. Plate: dense from the first moment, the brightest. Hall: big, smooth and chorused. Cathedral: huge, slow to bloom and dark.

params.label: Reverb decay
params.describes: How long the tail lasts (the time it takes to fall by 60 dB). Short is a space around the sound; long is a wash it sits in.

params.label: Reverb pre-delay
params.describes: How long the reverb waits before it starts. More keeps the note's attack clear in front of its space.

params.label: Reverb octave
params.describes: -1 shifts what goes into the reverb an octave down, so a note sinks into a huge, dark cloud an octave below itself (the reverb's Lo cut still keeps it off the low end).

params.label: Flanger low cut

params.describes: Where the band sits. Drag its ball sideways on the EQ's graph.

params.label: Grind 8 EQ 4 gain
params.describes: Boost or cut (shelf and bell only). Drag its ball up or down; 0 = flat.

params.label: Grind 8 EQ 4 Q
params.describes: How narrow the band is (or how steep a shelf, how resonant a pass filter). Scroll over the graph with its ball selected.

params.label: Grind 8 EQ scale
params.describes: Scales every band's gain: 100% as set, 0% flat, -100% the mirror image, up to ±200%.

params.label: Grind 8 width
params.describes: How wide the filter is: a wider notch or band, a broader peak, softer comb teeth and phaser notches. Down = narrow and sharp.

params.label: Grind 8 drive type
params.describes: The stage's drive after its filter: tape is soft and warm, its highs saturating first and rounded off; tube thick with even harmonics; amp a driven amp through a speaker cab, a close mic and a small room (boxy, biting, no low rumble or fizz on top); soft clip clean below its knee, rounding off the peaks. Then the hard ones: hard clip squares the peaks off flat; wavefold folds the wave back on itself, more folds the harder it is driven (metallic, glassy); rectify flips the bottom half up (the octave above, hollow and buzzy); downsample holds each sample longer as Drive goes up, down to 1/32 of the rate (gritty, aliased, digital); diode is lopsided, soft on top and clipping early below (snarling, uneven harmonics). Starved: a tube starved of current (the Culture Vulture trick): quiet parts sputter and gate, only the big swings get through, lopsided.

params.label: Grind 8 drive
params.describes: How hard the stage's drive is pushed (its level is matched, so more is dirtier, not louder). 0 = the filter only.

params.label: Grind 8 mix
params.describes: Blend between the filtered and the driven sound.

params.label: Grind 8 filter on
params.describes: The stage's moving filter on / off (keeps its settings): off, the stage is only its drive.

params.label: Grind 8 drive on
params.describes: The stage's drive on / off (keeps its settings): off, the stage is only its moving filter.

params.label: Grind 8 drive band
params.describes: Where the drive's band sits (as Ableton's Overdrive): only this band is distorted; the stage's Mix blends the untouched sound back in.

params.label: Grind 8 drive width
params.describes: How wide the drive's band is, in octaves: narrow distorts one area, 9 the whole sound.

params.label: Grind 8 drive tone
params.describes: After the distortion: low is dark and smooth, high keeps all the fizz (fully up = open).

params.label: Grind 8 drive dynamics
params.describes: How much of the playing's dynamics survives the distortion: low is squashed flat and dense, high keeps every swell and accent.

params.label: Drive band
params.describes: Where the drive's band sits (as Ableton's Overdrive): only this band is driven; Dry/Wet blends the untouched sound back in.

params.label: Drive width
params.describes: How wide the drive's band is, in octaves: narrow drives one area, 9 the whole sound.

params.label: Drive dynamics
params.describes: How much of the playing's dynamics survives the drive: low is squashed flat and dense, high keeps every swell and accent.

params.label: Drive output
params.describes: The drive's output level. The drive is pushed hot (more Drive is louder and denser); turn this down to bring the level back.
